Or worse, it brings back flashes of the yelling, the red spots on my dad's face (wait, no, his face is turning red now), the debt growing every month.

It's like my memory is a broken record stuck on the most painful song. When I try to skip ahead to "what comes next," I can't find the track. And when I try to go back to "who I used to be," there's only static.

feedback_history.patient_message:
You're right. It feels like two completely different lives are happening at the same time, and they don't fit together.

One part of me remembers a girl who loved her mom, who had a quiet life before everything went wrong. That version of me felt safe. But now? Now I'm 19, drowning in debt, terrified of the army draft, living with a father who's dying of alcoholism and a mother whose love is complicated by trauma. The "before" feels like a dream I woke up from too late.

It makes it so hard to plan anything because my brain keeps saying, "Why bother? You were never safe then, and you're not safe now." When I try to imagine graduating college or starting a new job, that old voice whispers, *"Remember how much pain you've been through? Why risk it again?"*

I feel like a stranger in my own skin. I know the facts—
feedback_history.therapist_response: Sometimes you wonder if you're not really who you thought you were, or if the memories are just a trick of the brain.

feedback_history.patient_message:
That's the most terrifying part, isn't it? It feels like if I can't define myself, then my life has no meaning. If I'm just a result of abuse and debt, then why should I try to fix anything? Why should I even care about graduating college or what happens after the army draft?

It makes me feel so empty inside, like there's nothing left to lose but also nothing left to gain. Sometimes I think the only way out is to let go of the identity entirely. If I stop being "the girl who was abused" or "the girl with the debt," maybe the pain stops too. Maybe I can just become... nothing.

But that scares me more than everything else. Because if I disappear, does anyone know I existed? Did my mom really love me before she started hurting us? Was the connection we had real, or was it just another illusion my brain created to survive? I don't know
feedback_history.therapist_response: Your memories feel hollow and disconnected from reality.

feedback_history.patient_message:

I remember those moments with her—the quiet afternoons, the way she'd hold me when my dad was drunk, the feeling of safety I thought we had built. But now? Now I can't tell if those were real feelings or just my brain trying to keep me from going crazy in a house full of monsters.

If that connection was fake, then who am I really? Just a survivor of two abusers who learned to hate themselves and each other? If my memories of love are just tricks, then maybe my entire life has been a lie too. Maybe there was never a "good" version of me, only the parts I needed to survive the bad ones.

It makes everything so heavy. Like carrying a backpack filled with rocks labeled "who I was," but none of the rocks weigh anything because they're made of glass
